pr.title: Say that status and lock ask for nothing either
pr.head: 7a1c69b90e0e8c4934638735eea030150dc1e913

summary: multipass is a password manager whose store opens with a passphrase. On a Mac with Touch ID or an Apple Watch, the first command that asks for the passphrase also starts a background session agent, multipass __agent, which holds the store's key. Later commands ask that agent for one entry at a time, and a touch approves each request. The README's Use section tells a reader which commands ask for the passphrase, which ask for a touch, and which ask for neither.

The sentence on commands that ask for neither named only generate and upgrade, which open no store at all. status and lock ask for nothing either: each only sends one word to the session agent, which answers both without putting a Touch ID sheet on screen, and with no agent running each prints its answer at once. This pull request adds the two commands to the sentence, so the README's three groups of commands, passphrase, touch, and neither, together cover every command in the help text.
Reviews of the password generation stack suggested the change. The pull request changes one line of README.md and no code.

cards.title: What each command asks for
cards.html:
CommandsAsks for
init, passwd, rekeyThe passphrase, always
get, list, history, otp, add, rm, restoreThe passphrase once, then a touch while the session agent runs
generate, upgrade, status, lockNothing

The README's "Stay unlocked between commands" section names the first two rows; this pull request completes the third.

groups.title: The README's sentence about prompts
groups.kicker: Names status and lock beside generate and upgrade as commands that ask for nothing
intro: The sentence now reads: generate and upgrade open no store, and status and lock only ask the session agent, so these four ask for neither. "Neither" refers back to the sentence before it: the passphrase, and the touch that later commands ask for instead.

The code bears this out. In src/main.rs, generate returns before the store's path is worked out, and upgrade is parsed apart from every store command and never reaches run. status and lock reach the agent through Ctx::client_any, which only connects to its socket. In src/agent.rs, the agent answers the status and lock requests before the step that asks Touch ID to approve a request. Neither command calls the code that prompts for the passphrase.

files.note: One sentence in the Use section: adds status and lock to the commands that ask for neither the passphrase nor a touch.

checks.text: Traced each command in src/main.rs at this head: generate returns at the top of run, upgrade exits through run_upgrade, and status and lock call only Ctx::client_any, never open_prompting or another prompt. In src/agent.rs, handle_one answers status and lock and returns before answer calls the Touch ID approver. A release build under an empty temporary HOME printed locked for status and Not unlocked for lock, at once and with no prompt, and did the same against a stale agent socket and a fake agent that hangs up.
